BeforeSideTurnStart.issue: Rollup of guards G1 and G2 per binding rule 4. The sim has no relic UI. Waived under the shared contract's presentation/animation exclusion, not under an unreachability claim.

guards.what: G1 (DORMANT): the sim binds C#'s BeforeSideTurnStart to on_player_turn_started -- turn_structure step 23, where the C# hook is step 9
guards.issue: MECHANISM: audit/records/seam/turn_structure.json puts Hook.BeforeSideTurnStart at step 9 (before any block is cleared, before the energy reset and before the enemies re-roll their moves at step 11) and Hook.AfterSideTurnStart at step 23 (after the hand draw). red_mask.py:19 sits on on_player_turn_started, the step-23 slot, so the Weak lands two slots later than the sim's OWN nearest counterpart (on_player_turn_start, step 19) and five steps later than C#. EXECUTED (`py audit/tools/relic_probes.py turn-order` plus `py audit/tools/relic_probes_b13.py red-mask`): the order is on_block_cleared -> on_energy_reset -> on_player_turn_start -> modify_hand_draw -> on_player_turn_started, and a spy listener installed for turn 2 confirms the enemy already carries Weak at every one of those points on a LATER turn while on turn 1 it cannot, because the relic itself is what applies it. IDENTICAL MECHANISM AND VERDICT as relic/bag_of_marbles G1 (batch 1), which the seam's own step-9 entry names alongside Red Mask. REACHABILITY (DORMANT): a live case needs a ported monster whose move selection reads its own Weak, or a ported turn-1 draw-time effect that reads enemy powers; the ported monsters branch on HP thresholds, turn counters and their own non-Weak powers. CORRECTION TO THE SEAM RECORD, reported in .superpowers/sdd/relic-batch-13-lessons.md: turn_structure step 9's dormancy rationale says 'every ported one is a per-turn counter reset or latch that does not read block or energy'. Red Mask is named in that same step's ported list and is NOT a counter reset -- it applies a debuff to every enemy. The verdict survives, but the stated reason does not cover this listener.

C# targets `Enemies.Where(e => e.IsHittable)`, and IsHittable is `!IsDead && Hook.ShouldAllowHitting(...)`. Relic.living_enemies() (relics/base.py:294-297) filters on `not e.is_gone` ONLY -- its own docstring concedes the should_allow_hitting predicate is applied by DamageCmd rather than here, and PowerCmd.apply does not apply it either (audit/records/seam/power_cmd.json gap G6, the missing CanReceivePowers backstop). So an alive-but-unhittable enemy receives Weak in the sim and is skipped by C#. SAME MECHANISM AND VERDICT as relic/bag_of_marbles G2, cited and matched per binding rule 3, including its dormancy evidence: the ported should_allow_hitting implementer gates on a mid-revival state (IllusionPower, powers.py) which cannot be true during turn 1's setup, the only turn Red Mask fires. Porting a turn-1 untargetable enemy makes it live. NOTE per binding rule 7: relics/base.py, powers.py and power_cmd.json are not hashed by this record.

guards.rationale: The participants check restricts a both-sides hook to the owner's own side turn; the sim's on_player_turn_started fires for the player only, so it is structurally satisfied. `self.turn <= 1` (red_mask.py:20) matches `TurnNumber <= 1` with the executed turn numbering (`py audit/tools/relic_probes.py turn-order` prints turn=1 for the first player turn). Note the source uses `<= 1` where relic/radiant_pearl in the same batch uses `== 1`; both partition identically because the counter starts at 1.

guards.what: N2: the multi-target `PowerCmd.Apply<WeakPower>(ctx, combatState.HittableEnemies, ...)` overload (RedMask.cs:28) vs the sim's per-enemy loop
guards.rationale: Both iterate the enemy list in index order and apply the same amount with the same applier (Owner.Creature / `applier=player`); the sim's loop makes the order explicit. The enemy SET is G2's subject, not this entry's. Same disposition as relic/bag_of_marbles N2.

guards.what: N3: WeakPower lands on ENEMIES, so PowerCmd.apply's player-side SkipNextDurationTick arm does not apply
guards.rationale: cmds.py:331-332 sets skip_next_tick only when `target.side == 'player'`, mirroring PowerCmd.Apply's `if (target.Side == CombatSide.Player && power.Type == PowerType.Debuff)` (PowerCmd.cs:144-147). Red Mask debuffs enemies, so the Weak ticks down at the end of the enemy side on both codebases and the relic's 1 Weak covers exactly the first enemy turn. Checked deliberately: had the sim applied the skip to enemies too, the relic would silently last a round longer. NOTE per binding rule 7: cmds.py and PowerCmd.cs are not hashed by this record.
